name: Sendara Contact Form
author: Jassim Mohammad

sections.description:
Sendara Contact Form adds one clean, secure contact form to your WordPress site. Visitors enter their full name, email address, subject and (optionally) a message, and it arrives in your inbox. That is the whole idea: no form builder to learn, no messages piling up in your database, no cookies and no tracking.

It is built for site owners who want a contact form that simply works, is easy for visitors to fill in, and does not create privacy or security headaches.

What visitors get

  • A short, clear form. Full name, email address and subject, plus a message box you can switch off. Every field has a visible label, and required fields are marked.
  • Instant feedback. Mistakes are shown next to the field as soon as the visitor tries to send, and the form sends without reloading the page.
  • Works without JavaScript. If JavaScript is off or blocked, the form still sends normally and shows the same messages after the page reloads.
  • Spell check. Spelling mistakes in the subject and message are underlined by the visitor’s own browser. It is private: nothing leaves their computer.
  • Optional grammar check. When you turn it on, a “Check spelling and grammar” button lists spelling, grammar and style suggestions that the visitor can apply with one click.
  • A copy of their message. A “Send me a copy of my message” checkbox emails the visitor what they sent.
  • Accessible. Errors are announced to screen readers and linked to their fields, focus moves to the first problem, everything works from the keyboard, and animations are turned off for people who prefer reduced motion.
  • Their language. All texts are translatable. Arabic is included, and the layout flips automatically for right-to-left languages.

What you get

  • Messages in your inbox. Each message is emailed to the address you choose, with the visitor set as Reply-To, so pressing Reply answers them directly.
  • Two ways to add the form. The “Sendara Contact Form” block for the block editor, or the [sendara_contact_form] shortcode for classic editors, widgets and page builders.
  • Spam protection without CAPTCHA. A hidden trap field, a minimum fill-in time and a security token are always on. An optional per-visitor limit stops floods. None of this uses cookies or bothers real visitors.
  • Reliable delivery. A “Send test email” button shows the exact reason if sending fails, and built-in SMTP lets you send through Gmail, Outlook, your host’s mailbox or an email service when your host does not deliver WordPress mail.
  • Delivery problems are reported. If a visitor’s message ever fails to send, the settings screen tells you when and why.
  • Optional GDPR consent checkbox, with your own text and a link to your privacy policy.
  • Privacy policy text written for you. The plugin adds suggested wording to the WordPress Privacy Policy Guide, matching the features you have turned on.
  • “Report a problem” screen to email the developer about a bug, with an optional preview of the technical details that will be included.
  • Clean uninstall. Deleting the plugin removes its settings and temporary counters, on every site of a multisite network.

Privacy at a glance

With the default settings, this plugin does not:

  • track visitors;
  • use cookies;
  • write visitors’ personal data to the database;
  • send any data to outside services.

Messages are emailed to you and are never saved on your website. The only features that involve another service are ones you choose to use: SMTP (emails pass through the provider you choose), the grammar check (text is sent to LanguageTool only when a visitor clicks the button) and “Report a problem” (an email to the developer, only when an administrator sends one). See “Privacy” and “External services” below for full details.

Security

The plugin follows WordPress security practice throughout:

  • every form and admin action is protected by a security token (nonce);
  • only administrators (users with the manage_options capability) can change settings, send test emails or send problem reports;
  • every input is sanitized and validated on the server, and every output is escaped;
  • line breaks are removed from anything placed in an email header, which blocks email header injection;
  • redirects only go to pages on your own site;
  • the SMTP password and LanguageTool API key are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using your site’s secret keys, and are never sent back to the browser;
  • grammar suggestions are shown as plain text, so nothing from the checking service can run code on your page;
  • the grammar service address cannot point at private or link-local network addresses;
  • email copies to visitors are limited to 3 per address per day;
  • no files are uploaded and nothing a visitor types is stored.

Usage

Adding the form

Block editor: open a page, click the + inserter, search for “Sendara Contact Form” (or “contact”, “form”, “email”) and add the block. The editor shows a live preview of the form.

Shortcode: paste [sendara_contact_form] into a Shortcode block, the classic editor, a text widget, or your page builder’s shortcode element (Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder and others).

Heading above the form: the shortcode accepts an optional title attribute, shown as a heading above the form:

[sendara_contact_form title="Get in touch"]

You can place the form on as many pages as you like, and even more than once on the same page. Every copy sends to the same address.

What the visitor sees

  • The fields Full name, Email address and Subject, and the Message box if it is turned on. All shown fields are required. Limits: name 100 characters, subject 150, message 5,000.
  • The consent checkbox, if you turned it on. The visitor must tick it to send.
  • The Send me a copy of my message checkbox, if it is on (it is on by default).
  • The Check spelling and grammar button under the message, if the grammar check is on.
  • After sending, your thank-you message, followed by a note saying whether their copy was sent.

Messages a visitor may see, and what they mean:

  • “Please check the highlighted fields and try again.” A field is empty, too long or not a valid email address.
  • “This form has expired. Please reload the page and try again.” The page’s security token is too old, usually because of page caching. See the FAQ.
  • “That was very quick! Please wait a few seconds and send the form again.” The form was sent less than 2 seconds after the page loaded, which is typical of bots.
  • “You have sent several messages in a short time.” The visitor reached the message limit.
  • “Sorry, your message could not be sent.” The email could not be sent. The reason is shown on your settings screen.

The email you receive

  • To: the Send messages to address (or the site administrator email).
  • From: your Sender name and Sender email settings (by default your site title and the WordPress default address).
  • Reply-To: the visitor’s name and email address.
  • Subject: your Subject prefix (by default [Your site title]) followed by the visitor’s subject.
  • Body: plain text with the name, email address, subject and message, the page the form was sent from, and the date and time.

The email is sent from your own site’s address rather than the visitor’s, because email providers treat a message “from” someone else’s Gmail or Outlook address as forged. Reply-To makes answering just as easy.

Settings

All settings are under Sendara Contact Form > Settings. Text fields left empty use a default that is translated automatically into your site language.

Where messages go

  • Send messages to: the address that receives messages. Empty uses the site administrator email.
  • Sender name: the name shown as the sender. Empty uses the site title.
  • Sender email: the address emails are sent from. Use an address on your own domain (for example info@yourdomain.com) or your SMTP login. Empty uses the SMTP username when SMTP is on and it is an email address, otherwise the WordPress default (wordpress@yourdomain).
  • Subject prefix: added before the visitor’s subject so you can filter these emails. Empty uses [Site title].

Form

  • Message field: show the message box under the subject. On by default.
  • Button text: the label of the send button. Empty uses “Send message”.
  • Thank-you message: shown after a message is sent. Empty uses “Thank you! Your message has been sent.”
  • Consent checkbox: ask visitors to agree before sending. Off by default.
  • Consent text: the text next to the consent checkbox. Links are allowed, so you can link to your privacy policy. Up to 500 characters.
  • Copy for the sender: show the “Send me a copy of my message” checkbox. On by default.

Spelling and grammar

  • Spell check: underline spelling mistakes in the subject and message using the visitor’s own browser. On by default. Nothing is sent anywhere.
  • Grammar check: show a “Check spelling and grammar” button. Off by default. When a visitor clicks it, their message text is sent from your server to the checking service below.
  • Checking service: the LanguageTool address. Leave it as is for LanguageTool’s free public service (https://api.languagetool.org/v2/check), or enter the address of LanguageTool Premium or your own LanguageTool server (for example http://localhost:8081/v2/check).
  • LanguageTool username and LanguageTool API key: only for LanguageTool Premium. The key is stored encrypted.

Spam protection

The hidden trap field, the 2-second minimum fill-in time and the security token are always on.

  • Limit messages: limit how many messages one visitor can send in 10 minutes. On by default.
  • Messages per 10 minutes: between 1 and 100. Default 5.

Email delivery (SMTP)

Turn this on if test emails do not arrive. It affects only this plugin’s emails, never other plugins or WordPress itself.

  • Use SMTP: send this plugin’s emails through the server below.
  • SMTP server: for example smtp.gmail.com, smtp.office365.com or your host’s mail server.
  • Port: usually 587 with TLS, or 465 with SSL.
  • Encryption: TLS, SSL or None (not recommended).
  • Authentication: whether the server needs a username and password (almost always yes).
  • Username: usually your full email address.
  • Password: stored encrypted; leave empty to keep the saved one. For Gmail, use an App Password.

Test email and delivery errors

The Check that email works box sends a test email to any address you enter, using your saved settings. If sending fails, the exact reason is shown (with the password removed). If a visitor’s message ever fails to send, a notice on the settings screen shows when it happened and why; it disappears after the next successful email.

Spelling and grammar check

Spell check uses the spell checker built into the visitor’s browser, in the browser’s language. It is completely private.

Grammar check uses LanguageTool, which detects the language automatically and supports more than 30 languages, including English, Arabic, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Dutch. It finds grammar, punctuation and style problems as well as spelling.

How it works:

  1. The visitor writes their message and clicks Check spelling and grammar.
  2. Your server sends the text to the checking service. The request comes from your server, so the visitor’s IP address and browser details are not passed on.
  3. Up to 50 suggestions are listed. The visitor can click a replacement to apply it, or Ignore to dismiss it.
  4. If the visitor edits the text after checking, they are asked to check again, so a fix can never land in the wrong place.

Each visitor can run up to 20 checks per 10 minutes. The free public LanguageTool service also has its own limit (about 20 requests per minute for your whole site). If the service does not answer, the visitor sees “The spelling and grammar check is not available right now.” and can still send their message.

To keep all text on your own servers, run a self-hosted LanguageTool server (free and open source) and enter its address as Checking service. Addresses on the same machine (localhost, 127.0.0.1) are allowed. Other addresses must be public http or https addresses on a standard port (80, 443 or 8080); private network addresses are refused.

Privacy

What is stored. Only the plugin settings, in one option (sendara_cf_settings), plus short-lived counters and notices in WordPress transients. No message, name or email address from a visitor is ever written to the database.

Messages. Sent by email to the site owner only. If you turn on SMTP, emails pass through the SMTP provider you choose (for example Google or Microsoft); check that provider’s privacy policy.

Message limit. When “Limit messages” is on, a keyed one-way hash of the visitor’s IP address is used as the name of a counter that lasts up to 10 minutes and is then deleted automatically. The IP address itself is never stored. The grammar check uses the same kind of counter for its 20-checks limit.

Copies. When a visitor asks for a copy, a keyed one-way hash of their email address is used as the name of a counter that lasts up to 24 hours (to enforce the 3-copies-a-day limit) and is then deleted automatically.

Grammar check. Off by default. When on, the visitor’s message text is sent to the checking service each time they click “Check spelling and grammar”, and a note under the button tells them so. Nothing is sent if they do not click.

Delivery errors. The reason for the last failed email is kept for up to 7 days so it can be shown to you. Email addresses and the SMTP password are removed from it.

Cookies. The plugin sets no cookies.

Privacy policy text. The plugin adds suggested text to Settings > Privacy > Policy Guide that matches your settings (for example, it mentions copies and the grammar check only when they are turned on). Copy it into your own privacy policy. You remain responsible for your privacy policy and for how you handle the emails you receive.

External services

This plugin connects to outside services only in the cases below. None of them is used with the default settings, except “Report a problem”, which runs only when an administrator sends a report.

LanguageTool (grammar check)

  • What it is: an online spelling, grammar and style checker, run by LanguageTooler GmbH, Germany.
  • When it is used: only if an administrator turns on Grammar check, and only when a visitor clicks Check spelling and grammar.
  • What is sent: the text of the visitor’s message, the setting language=auto, and, for LanguageTool Premium, your LanguageTool username and API key. The visitor’s IP address and browser details are not sent.
  • Where it goes: https://api.languagetool.org/v2/check by default, or the address you enter in Checking service.
  • Terms of service: https://languagetool.org/legal/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://languagetool.org/legal/privacy

sections.installation:
Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or newer.
  • PHP 7.4 or newer.
  • A way to send email: either your host’s normal WordPress mail, or an SMTP account (Gmail, Outlook, your host’s mailbox or an email service).
  • The OpenSSL PHP extension, only if you want to save an SMTP password or LanguageTool API key in the settings. It is present on almost every host.

Install from your dashboard

  1. Go to Plugins > Add New Plugin and search for “Sendara Contact Form”, or click Upload Plugin and upload sendara-contact-form.zip.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.

Install manually

  1. Unzip the file and upload the sendara-contact-form folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin on the Plugins screen.

Set it up in three steps

  1. Go to Sendara Contact Form > Settings, enter the address that should receive messages in Send messages to, and click Save Changes. If you leave it empty, messages go to the site administrator email in Settings > General.
  2. In the Check that email works box, click Send test email and confirm it arrives (check the spam folder too). If it does not, see “I am not receiving messages” in the FAQ.
  3. Add the Sendara Contact Form block to your contact page, or paste the shortcode [sendara_contact_form]. The settings screen has a Copy button for the shortcode.
sections.faq:
How do I add the form to my site?

Add the Sendara Contact Form block in the block editor, or paste [sendara_contact_form] anywhere shortcodes work. You can copy the shortcode from Sendara Contact Form > Settings.

Where do the messages go?

To the address in Send messages to. If that is empty, they go to the site administrator email in Settings > General.

Can I send messages to more than one address?

Not from the settings screen. Set up forwarding in your email account, or use the sendara_cf_recipient_email filter to return several comma-separated addresses.

Can I add or remove fields?

You can switch off the message box, and add or remove the consent and copy checkboxes. The plugin deliberately keeps to these fields so it stays simple and secure; it is not a form builder.

I am not receiving messages

  1. Save your settings, then click Send test email on the settings screen.
  2. If it says the email could not be sent, read the reason. “Could not authenticate” means a wrong SMTP username or password; “Could not connect” means a wrong server, port or encryption.
  3. If it says your server accepted the email but nothing arrives (check spam too), your host is not delivering WordPress mail. Turn on Use SMTP, enter your email provider’s details, save and test again.
  4. Check that Send messages to is spelled correctly.

How do I send through Gmail?

Server smtp.gmail.com, port 587, encryption TLS, your full Gmail address as username, and a Google App Password (not your normal password) as password. App Passwords need 2-Step Verification in your Google account. Leave Sender email empty so your Gmail address is used as the sender.

I already use WP Mail SMTP or a similar plugin. Do I need the SMTP settings here?

No. Leave Use SMTP off and your existing SMTP plugin sends the form’s emails as usual.

Is my SMTP password safe?

It is stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with a key made from your site’s secret keys, it is never shown again in the dashboard or in error messages, and only administrators can change it. To keep it out of the database entirely, define SENDARA_CF_SMTP_PASSWORD in wp-config.php. If you change your site’s secret keys, enter the password again.

Visitors see “This form has expired”

A caching plugin or CDN is serving an old copy of the page, and its security token has expired. Exclude the contact page from page caching, or make cached pages refresh at least every 10 hours. Other WordPress form plugins have the same requirement.

Everyone hits the message limit at once

Your site is probably behind a proxy or CDN (such as Cloudflare), so all visitors seem to share one IP address. Untick Limit messages, or use the sendara_cf_client_ip filter (see “For developers”).

Do I need reCAPTCHA?

Usually not. The trap field, minimum fill-in time and security token stop most automated spam without bothering real visitors. If you still receive spam, lower Messages per 10 minutes, turn on the consent checkbox, or add a CAPTCHA through the sendara_cf_before_send filter. CAPTCHA services send visitor data to their provider, so mention one in your privacy policy.

Could someone use “Send me a copy” to spam other people?

The plugin guards against it: each address receives at most 3 copies a day, a copy is only sent after the message passed every spam check, and the copy contains only what was typed plus a line saying it can be ignored if the recipient did not send it. You can also turn the feature off.

Does it store messages?

No. Messages are only emailed. Keep the emails if you need a record.

Does it use cookies or track visitors?

No.

Is it GDPR-friendly?

It is designed to be: personal data only travels to your inbox, you can require a consent checkbox, and suggested privacy policy text is provided. You remain responsible for your own privacy policy and for how you handle the emails.

Why is the grammar check off by default?

Because it sends what the visitor wrote to an outside service, and the plugin does not do that unless you choose to.

Does the grammar check cost anything?

The public LanguageTool service is free and needs no account. Busy sites can use LanguageTool Premium (enter the username and API key) or run their own free LanguageTool server.

Which languages are included?

English and Arabic. The plugin follows your site language automatically and supports right-to-left layouts. To translate it into another language, use translate.wordpress.org, Loco Translate or Poedit with the included languages/sendara-contact-form.pot file.

Does it work with WPML or Polylang?

It uses the standard WordPress translation system, so built-in texts follow the page language. Custom texts you type in the settings are shown exactly as typed in every language; leave them empty to get automatic translation.

Does it work without JavaScript?

Yes. The page reloads after sending and shows the same messages.

Does it work with page builders?

Yes. Use the builder’s shortcode element with [sendara_contact_form].

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Each site has its own settings, and deleting the plugin cleans up every site.

How do I report a bug?

Go to Sendara Contact Form > Report a problem, describe what happened and click Send report. You can preview the technical details before sending.

What happens to my settings if I delete the plugin?

Deactivating keeps them. Deleting the plugin from the Plugins screen removes its settings (including the encrypted password and API key) and all temporary counters. No messages are stored, so nothing else is left behind.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • Change: renamed to Sendara Contact Form. The shortcode is now [sendara_contact_form] and the block is “Sendara Contact Form”.
  • Change: Plugin URI is https://jeemplugins.com/plugins/sendara-contact-form/.

1.2.1

  • Fix: Plugin URI points to the plugin’s own homepage.
  • Change: removed the manual translation loader; WordPress loads the bundled translations itself.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.1.
  • Docs: the readme now documents every setting, the external services the plugin can use, and the developer hooks.

1.2.0

  • New: “Send me a copy of my message” checkbox, with a per-address daily limit.
  • New: browser spell check on the subject and message (can be turned off).
  • New: optional spelling and grammar check through LanguageTool or a self-hosted LanguageTool server, with one-click fixes.
  • Fix: an email address containing illegal characters was silently changed into a different address instead of being rejected.
  • Fix: the privacy policy suggestion now matches the features that are turned on.
  • Hardening: the grammar service address cannot point at private or link-local network addresses.

1.1.0

  • New: built-in SMTP sending with encrypted password storage.
  • New: “Sender email” setting, and the envelope sender now matches the From address for better delivery.
  • New: test email can go to any address and shows the exact error when it fails; failed visitor emails are reported on the settings screen.
  • New: “Report a problem” is set up to reach the developer and uses the same delivery settings.
  • Fix: the visitor’s name appeared with extra quotes in the Reply-To header.
  • Fix: the test email used the saved recipient even when a new one had just been typed.
  • Fix: duplicate button ID on the settings screen.
  • Fix: the hidden spam-trap field could be filled in by browser autofill, silently dropping real messages.
  • Fix: the form failed with “connection problem” on sites where only the admin area uses HTTPS.
  • Fix: a long consent text could be cut in the middle of a link.

1.0.0

  • First release.

  • Checking service: the LanguageTool address. Leave it as is for LanguageTool’s free public service (https://api.languagetool.org/v2/check), or enter the address of LanguageTool Premium or your own LanguageTool server (for example http://localhost:8081/v2/check).
  • LanguageTool username and LanguageTool API key: only for LanguageTool Premium. The key is stored encrypted.

Spam protection

The hidden trap field, the 2-second minimum fill-in time and the security token are always on.

  • Limit messages: limit how many messages one visitor can send in 10 minutes. On by default.
  • Messages per 10 minutes: between 1 and 100. Default 5.

Email delivery (SMTP)

Turn this on if test emails do not arrive. It affects only this plugin’s emails, never other plugins or WordPress itself.

  • Use SMTP: send this plugin’s emails through the server below.
  • SMTP server: for example smtp.gmail.com, smtp.office365.com or your host’s mail server.
  • Port: usually 587 with TLS, or 465 with SSL.
  • Encryption: TLS, SSL or None (not recommended).
  • Authentication: whether the server needs a username and password (almost always yes).
  • Username: usually your full email address.
  • Password: stored encrypted; leave empty to keep the saved one. For Gmail, use an App Password.

Test email and delivery errors

The Check that email works box sends a test email to any address you enter, using your saved settings. If sending fails, the exact reason is shown (with the password removed). If a visitor’s message ever fails to send, a notice on the settings screen shows when it happened and why; it disappears after the next successful email.

Spelling and grammar check

Spell check uses the spell checker built into the visitor’s browser, in the browser’s language. It is completely private.

Grammar check uses LanguageTool, which detects the language automatically and supports more than 30 languages, including English, Arabic, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Dutch. It finds grammar, punctuation and style problems as well as spelling.

How it works:

  1. The visitor writes their message and clicks Check spelling and grammar.
  2. Your server sends the text to the checking service. The request comes from your server, so the visitor’s IP address and browser details are not passed on.
  3. Up to 50 suggestions are listed. The visitor can click a replacement to apply it, or Ignore to dismiss it.
  4. If the visitor edits the text after checking, they are asked to check again, so a fix can never land in the wrong place.

Each visitor can run up to 20 checks per 10 minutes. The free public LanguageTool service also has its own limit (about 20 requests per minute for your whole site). If the service does not answer, the visitor sees “The spelling and grammar check is not available right now.” and can still send their message.

To keep all text on your own servers, run a self-hosted LanguageTool server (free and open source) and enter its address as Checking service. Addresses on the same machine (localhost, 127.0.0.1) are allowed. Other addresses must be public http or https addresses on a standard port (80, 443 or 8080); private network addresses are refused.

Privacy

What is stored. Only the plugin settings, in one option (sendara_cf_settings), plus short-lived counters and notices in WordPress transients. No message, name or email address from a visitor is ever written to the database.

Messages. Sent by email to the site owner only. If you turn on SMTP, emails pass through the SMTP provider you choose (for example Google or Microsoft); check that provider’s privacy policy.

Message limit. When “Limit messages” is on, a keyed one-way hash of the visitor’s IP address is used as the name of a counter that lasts up to 10 minutes and is then deleted automatically. The IP address itself is never stored. The grammar check uses the same kind of counter for its 20-checks limit.

Copies. When a visitor asks for a copy, a keyed one-way hash of their email address is used as the name of a counter that lasts up to 24 hours (to enforce the 3-copies-a-day limit) and is then deleted automatically.

Grammar check. Off by default. When on, the visitor’s message text is sent to the checking service each time they click “Check spelling and grammar”, and a note under the button tells them so. Nothing is sent if they do not click.

Delivery errors. The reason for the last failed email is kept for up to 7 days so it can be shown to you. Email addresses and the SMTP password are removed from it.

Cookies. The plugin sets no cookies.

Privacy policy text. The plugin adds suggested text to Settings > Privacy > Policy Guide that matches your settings (for example, it mentions copies and the grammar check only when they are turned on). Copy it into your own privacy policy. You remain responsible for your privacy policy and for how you handle the emails you receive.

External services

This plugin connects to outside services only in the cases below. None of them is used with the default settings, except “Report a problem”, which runs only when an administrator sends a report.

LanguageTool (grammar check)

  • What it is: an online spelling, grammar and style checker, run by LanguageTooler GmbH, Germany.
  • When it is used: only if an administrator turns on Grammar check, and only when a visitor clicks Check spelling and grammar.
  • What is sent: the text of the visitor’s message, the setting language=auto, and, for LanguageTool Premium, your LanguageTool username and API key. The visitor’s IP address and browser details are not sent.
  • Where it goes: https://api.languagetool.org/v2/check by default, or the address you enter in Checking service.
  • Terms of service: https://languagetool.org/legal/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://languagetool.org/legal/privacy
